entries.EN:
The SIG Sauer P320 is a modular semi-automatic pistol manufactured by the American subsidiary of SIG Sauer Inc. This is a further development of the SIG Sauer P250, which uses a striker-type trigger. The P320 can use 9x19mm Parabellum, .357 SIG, .40 S&W, .45 ACP and 10mm Auto cartridges. The P320 chambered in 9?19mm Parabellum was introduced to the US market on January 15, 2014, followed by a compact model chambered in .45 ACP introduced at the SHOT Show in January 2015. On January 19, 2017, a modified SIG Sauer version was announced The P320 won the US Army's XM17 Modular Pistol System competition. Adopted into service under the designation M17. 
 

		%c[0,255,255,255]PROPERTIES:

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Origin: %c[0,170,170,170]United States

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Manufacturer: %c[0,170,170,170]SIG Sauer Inc.
entries.JA_current:
SIG Sauerの米国子会社が製造する、モジュール式の半自動拳銃。ストライカー方式の撃発機構を採用し、SIG Sauer P250を発展させたモデルだ。9×19mmパラベラム、.357 SIG、.40 S&W、.45 ACP、10mm Auto弾を使用できる。9×19mm仕様は2014年1月15日に米国市場へ登場し、2015年1月のSHOT Showでは.45 ACP仕様のコンパクトモデルが発表された。2017年1月19日には改良型が発表され、米陸軍のXM17モジュラー拳銃システム選定で採用された。軍ではM17の名称で配備されている。
 

		%c[0,255,255,255]特性：

		%c[0,255,255,255] • 原産： %c[0,170,170,170]アメリカ合衆国

		%c[0,255,255,255] • 製造元： %c[0,170,170,170]SIG Sauer Inc.

entries.EN:
OTs-33 "Pernach" (Russian for multivaned mace) is a recent entry into the small class of Russian automatic pistols. The OTs-33 is a blowback-operated weapon firing the 9x18mm Makarov pistol cartridge in automatic and semi-automatic mode. The Pernach was developed in 1995 to replace the Stechkin APS pistol in special paramilitary units. Designed in 1995 by Igor Stechkin at the TSKIB SOO, Central Design Bureau for Sporting and Hunting arms, Tula, Russia, the same designer who developed the APS.
 

		%c[0,255,255,255]PROPERTIES:

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Origin: %c[0,170,170,170]Russia

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Manufacturer: %c[0,170,170,170]KBP Instrument Design Bureau

entries.EN:
A single-action, semi-automatic pistol based on the ideas of American firearms inventor John Browning. Browning died in 1926 before finishing a production version, but FN arms designer Dieudonne Saive completed the pistol's development. The Hi-Power pistol was noted for its 13-round magazine, twice that of contemporary designs such as the Luger or Mauser 1910. Despite its venerable age, the Browning HP enjoys popularity around the world.
 

		%c[0,255,255,255]PROPERTIES:

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Origin: %c[0,170,170,170]Belgium, United States

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Manufacturer: %c[0,170,170,170]Browning Arms, FN Herstal

entries.EN:
A gas-operated, semi-automatic pistol known for chambering the largest cartridge of any magazine-fed, self-loading pistol. It uses a gas-operated ejection/chambering mechanism normally only found in rifles, allowing it to use far more powerful cartridges than traditional semi-automatic pistol designs. This allows the Desert Eagle to compete in an area that had previously been dominated by Magnum revolvers.

entries.EN:
The Fort-12 is an attempt for recently-independent Ukrain (from August 1991) to create its own police pistol to replace the Soviet-era Makarov PM, while still using the same 9x18 caliber. Designed in 1995 and developed in 1998 by Ukrainian firearms designer RPC Fort, this is a formidable pistol considered to be an upgrade of the PM itself. Although it may have reliability issues, especially due to the lack of the safe decocking facility, it compensates for the accuracy, magizine and ergonomics. This model comes with a threaded barrel, allowing it to equip silencers by default.
 

		%c[0,255,255,255]PROPERTIES:

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Origin: %c[0,170,170,170]Ukraine

		%c[0,255,255,255] • Manufacturer: %c[0,170,170,170]RPC Fort

entries.EN:
A gas-operated, semi-automatic pistol known for chambering the largest cartridge of any magazine-fed, self-loading pistol. It uses a gas-operated ejection/chambering mechanism normally only found in rifles, allowing it to use far more powerful cartridges than traditional semi-automatic pistol designs. This allows the Desert Eagle to compete in an area that had previously been dominated by Magnum revolvers. The "Steppe Eagle" features an integrated muzzle compensator for drastically reduced recoil and a heavily redesigned picatinny rail for use with a range of sights and scopes. Apparently brought to the Zone by a Stalker, fate unknown, under the guise of a journalist-photographer who managed to reach the center of Pripyat alone.

entries.EN:
Developed as a more powerful, lighter and cheaper successor to the MP5, the UMP45 provides greater stopping power but also produces more recoil. To mitigate this issue, the UMP's cyclic rate of fire was lowered significantly. Though created to replace the MP5, both submachine guns still see production to this day with the UMP being used in more than 20 countries, worldwide.
